keyFindings.text: **REQ-004's mechanics, verbatim source**: ask only when (a) there is no prompt AND no task description, (b) two mode commands conflict, or (c) the request is not prompt work and needs one reframe. Everything else is a "soft gap" with a default → numbered `### Open items` after the deliverable (bold topic + `- **Situation:**`/`- **Open:**` bullets, `None identified` when empty). After 3 unresolved clarifications → smart defaults as open items. Open items never sit inside the prompt — sk-prompt's `[Assumes: X]` in-prompt convention is the opposite design choice. keyFindings.text: **REQ-005's implementation template exists and is more precise than the REQ**: `strip_source_prompt()` strips fenced blocks (``` or ~~~), then quoted spans of ≥3 words (1-2 word quotes stay — the user naming a platform), else the text after a `prompt:`-style lead-in up to the next blank line; returns `(own_text, has_source)`. Commands match whole `$[a-z]+` tokens only; ≥2 distinct mode commands is a conflict → INTERACTIVE fallback; keywords score on word boundaries; a bare pasted prompt routes IMPROVE. keyFindings.text: **REQ-002 validated, with a sharper checklist than the REQ names.** Anthropic's live page still carries "Prefer general instructions over prescriptive steps" and "verify your answer against [test criteria]" — the one-pass check + self-check shape is the vendor-endorsed form. The closest public analog (christabone) runs exactly REQ-002's protocol: a fixed ~10-technique list, per-item present?/benefit?/how-to-apply verdicts with 1-2 sentence rationale in visible `<thinking>`, mixed script checks (XML tags, variables) and judgment checks, then the rewrite, then a summary. Its component set differs from REQ-002's — it has variables, chain-of-thought and task-decomposition but no success-criteria, contradiction or model-fit rows — so checklist membership is a design choice, the one-pass-verdict protocol is the invariant. [SOURCE: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices (lines ~490,780,783); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/christabone/claude-prompt-improvement/main/skills/improve-prompt/CHECKLIST.md; .../SKILL.md]

keyFindings.text: **REQ-003 validated by two independent pass-through designs.** severity1's hook spends ~189 tokens evaluating every prompt and proceeds immediately on clear ones ("zero skill overhead"), asking 1-6 grounded questions only on vague ones; OpenAI's meta-prompt orders "Minimal Changes: improve it only if it's simple … without altering the original structure"; christabone bans "over-engineer prompts that are already effective" and per-technique "Skip if" rows. A prompt that already passes gets minimal edits — convergent. keyFindings.text: **REQ-004 validated with one boundary caveat.** Vendor improvers ask nothing (OpenAI meta-prompt takes taskOrPrompt and emits; christabone edits in place); the sibling's deliver-first+open-items matches them. But severity1 shows a third defensible model — evaluate, pass on clear, ask grounded questions on vague — "only ask when genuinely unclear; never block." So "deliver first, ask only when nothing can be defaulted" is right for sk-prompt's stated goals, while an *ask-when-vague* mode is the honest alternative to name, not dismiss. [SOURCE: severity1 README design philosophy; OpenAI meta-prompt; iteration-2 findings]

keyFindings.text: **REQ-008 validated — and OpenAI's own meta-prompt IS the counter-example to framework sprawl.** Its output contract is one fixed skeleton (concise instruction → details → optional #Steps → #Output Format → #Examples → #Notes). No surveyed vendor names acronym frameworks; all describe components (role/context/task/examples/format/constraints). The seven sk-prompt frameworks collapse into one skeleton; keeping names as internal labels at most is consistent with agent-contract compatibility (FRAMEWORK field still emits a name). Caveat carried from iteration 1: `framework-registry.json` is benchmark scaffold, so the acceptance criterion should target SKILL.md §3 + patterns-evaluation.md §2, not that file. keyFindings.text: **REQ-009 mostly validated; the "3 to 5 examples" count is too confident.** Anthropic says 3-5 varied examples in `<example>` tags; OpenAI's skeleton says 1-3 with placeholders; Gemini says always few-shot but "experiment with the number" and warns of overfitting. A range with a default (≥1, typical ~3, up to 5 for complex tasks) is more defensible than a fixed 3-5. The contradiction check is supported by Anthropic's correctness/zero-contradiction language and OpenAI's reasoning-order rules; the plain-language rule is verbatim Anthropic ("CRITICAL: You MUST…" → "Use this tool when…"). Treating `framework-registry.json` as the framework *selection* surface REQ-008 implies: it is benchmark scaffold data; the selection surface is SKILL.md §3's matrix + patterns-evaluation §2. [evidence: finding 7]

`benchmark/router/` is NOT inside `sk-prompt-improver/` — it lives at the project root.
